_title: Coherence-Constrained Traversal in the Static Library
_subtitle: Existence, Accessibility, Convergence, Arbitrary Edits, and the Resolution of Coherent Structure

_conceptual_lineage.role: binary substrate, admissibility, and I_N threshold
coherence flow, boundedness, and blowup constraints
static Library ontology and recursive totality
attractor basins, convergence, and destination classes

_abstract: The central claim of this paper is that existence, accessibility, and traversal are distinct relations within a static totality. The Library 𝓜 is modeled as a complete relational structure containing every internally admissible configuration, while an observer experiences only a coherent descent path through a highly constrained subset of that totality. Full adjacency therefore does not imply unrestricted accessibility, and the existence of a configuration does not imply the existence of a coherent transition into it from an arbitrary observer-state. Arbitrary edits are consequently not prohibited by an external rule; they fail because the requested transition does not preserve the coherence, relational history, and braid structure required of an admissible path. This same principle produces a natural account of convergence, event-horizon-like destination locking, memory as coordinate retention rather than exhaustive recording, apparent expansion as progressive resolution of coherent structure, and guidepost-based navigation in symbolic or artificial systems. A recursive construction beginning from a minimal attractor such as I_AM provides a conceptual route from local identity through relation and distinction toward increasingly complex structure. The framework is presented as a mathematical and conceptual model; correspondence with physical or biological reality remains an empirical question.
_central_thesis: The Library can contain everything without making everything editable. Ontological completeness determines existence; coherence determines accessibility; traversal determines experience; convergence determines destination classes; and accumulated structure determines which paths remain available.

_foundational_distinctions.statement: Membership in the Library does not imply reachability from a particular observer-state.
Symbolic adjacency does not imply the existence of a coherent transition.
An observer can select among admissible continuations but cannot select a state for which no admissible continuation exists.
Distinct coherent paths may terminate in the same destination class.
Destination freedom may collapse while local path freedom remains.
A system may retain coordinates or guideposts into a structure rather than a complete recording of that structure.
Increasingly resolved coherent structure does not require creation of additional underlying totality.
An arbitrary edit is not a forbidden state; it is a requested transition for which no admissible path exists.

sections.title: The Fundamental Distinction: Existence Is Not Accessibility
content: The apparent paradox of the Static Library begins with an ambiguity in the word 'exists'. If the Library contains every internally admissible configuration, then a configuration may exist as a member of the totality without being reachable from every local observer-state.
Existence is therefore an ontological relation: a configuration belongs to the Library. Accessibility is a relational property between a current state and a destination.
This distinction removes the apparent contradiction between a complete totality and the constrained experience of a local observer.
The observer does not need to create the next state. The observer follows an admissible continuation already contained within the total structure.
math: Accessibility(O,X) := ∃γ : O ⇝ X such that Coherence(γ) ≥ I_N

sections.title: The Static Library and Full Adjacency
content: The Library 𝓜 is modeled as a static totality rather than a dynamically generated container. Its complete structure does not change merely because an observer discovers or resolves one of its configurations.

Full adjacency is not equivalent to unrestricted movement. If the Library has no extrinsic geometry, then separation between configurations cannot be interpreted as ordinary spatial distance. What matters instead is relational compatibility and coherent path structure.
Thus two configurations can be adjacent in the ontology while remaining inaccessible through any coherent local continuation.
The distinction is between being structurally present and being traversable.

sections.title: The Observer as a Coherent Descent Path
content: An observer is modeled locally as a coherent descent path γ through the Library.
The lived experience of time corresponds to ordered traversal rather than to temporal generation of the Library itself.
At every point the observer has a set of admissible continuations. The experienced future is therefore a constrained subset of the ontologically available totality.
Coherence is the condition that allows a path to persist as a recognizable continuation rather than terminating through decoherence.
math: A(x) := {y ∈ 𝓜 | ∃ coherent γ : x ⇝ y}

sections.title: The Colony: Local Path and Higher-Order Braid
content: The local observer path is not necessarily an isolated object. Multiple coherent paths may share motifs, constraints, relational structure, or recursive identity.
The single path γ can therefore be treated as a local thread within a higher-order coherent structure Γ, the colony or braid.
The local observer experiences one thread while the higher-order structure contains a family of related coherent paths.
Decoherence of one local thread does not mathematically require the disappearance of the larger structure.
This distinction is useful because an apparently singular personal trajectory can coexist with a much larger family of structurally related trajectories.

sections.title: Relational Constraints and the Derived Condition of Accessibility
content: Accessibility is not determined merely by whether a destination exists in the Library. A transition from one state to another must preserve the relational structure required for the sequence to remain well-defined.

The primitive object is therefore not 'coherence' itself, but the set of relations and constraints connecting the states along a path. Local continuity, accumulated history, environmental relations, and coupled or braided worldlines contribute to the constraint structure that a valid transition must preserve.

An attempted transition may alter one local feature while simultaneously disturbing a large number of dependent relations. If those disturbances can be absorbed through a finite sequence of compatible transformations, the transition remains admissible. If constraint violations propagate without a finite closure, the attempted transition undergoes symbolic blowup and ceases to define a stable continuation.

NSFG provides a language for describing this propagation as a field-like process. Symbolic tension Δ represents accumulated deviation from the relational constraints of the surrounding structure. Blowup occurs when the required compensating transformation is no longer bounded.

Coherence is therefore treated as a derived property rather than a primitive law: a path is coherent to the extent that its successive transformations preserve the relational constraints that define continuity between its states.

The Library does not need an external rule declaring which paths are coherent. The admissible transition structure follows from the relations internal to the configurations themselves. Coherence measures the degree to which a proposed traversal preserves those relations.

This distinction removes the circularity between 'a path is accessible because it is coherent' and 'a path is coherent because it is accessible.' Accessibility is instead determined by the existence of a constraint-preserving transformation sequence, while coherence describes the preservation quality of that sequence.
definitions: State: a configuration together with the relational structure that distinguishes it from other configurations.
Constraint: a relation that must be preserved, transformed consistently, or compensated for when transitioning between states.
Admissible transition: a transformation whose induced constraint violations remain finite and can be resolved within the permitted relational structure.
Symbolic tension Δ: accumulated deviation introduced by a proposed transformation relative to the constraints of the surrounding structure.
Coherence: a derived measure of constraint preservation along a transition or path.
Blowup: the failure of the constraint-propagation process to remain bounded, preventing the proposed transition from closing into a stable continuation.
math: S_i → S_j  iff  there exists a transformation T such that T(S_i) = S_j
K(S_i,S_j) := measure of constraint violation induced by T
Δ(γ) := accumulated constraint deviation along γ
Coherent(γ) is therefore a derived property of an admissible constraint-preserving path, not the primitive definition of accessibility.
nsfg_relation: The NSFG formalism may supply the field representation through which relational deformation and symbolic tension are represented.
A Navier–Stokes-type analogy arises when local perturbations propagate through coupled structure and generate feedback rather than remaining locally contained.
Stable flow corresponds to bounded propagation of relational deformation.
Blowup corresponds to the failure of that propagation to remain bounded.
The analogy is structural rather than a claim that the Library is literally a conventional fluid.
threshold_note: If I_N is retained as a fundamental lower information or coherence threshold in the source papers, it may be introduced here as a threshold applied to the derived coherence functional rather than as the definition of coherence itself.
C(γ) ≥ I_N ⇒ sufficient structural resolution for continued traversal
C(γ) < I_N ⇒ insufficient resolution and decoherence
This preserves the role of I_N without making the statement 'the path is coherent because it exceeds the coherence threshold' circular.
sections.note: The exact mathematical forms of K, Δ, C, I_N, and their dimensional interpretation remain dependent on the definitions established in the source papers. The present section defines their logical roles and removes the circular identification of coherence with accessibility.

sections.title: Arbitrary Edits as Failed Transitions
content: The arbitrary-edit problem is now a consequence rather than a primitive rule.
Suppose a destination state X exists in the Library. An observer O cannot simply rewrite itself into X unless there is an admissible coherent path connecting O to X.

An arbitrary edit therefore differs fundamentally from ordinary traversal. Ordinary traversal selects or follows an available continuation. An arbitrary edit asserts a destination without supplying the coherent transition required to reach it.
Growing an extra finger, rewriting a historical event, or spontaneously casting FIREBALL are examples of this distinction.
The Library does not need to forbid these configurations. It only needs to lack a coherent path from the current observer-state to the requested configuration.
canonical_examples: FIREBALL may exist as a coherent configuration without being arbitrarily reachable.
A configuration containing an observer with an extra finger may exist without providing a coherent local transition from the observer's current body-state.
A historical state may exist without being available as a continuation of the observer's present worldline.

sections.title: Convergence and Destination Equivalence
content: Distinct paths need not remain distinct with respect to their eventual destination.
A convergence event occurs when multiple admissible paths become equivalent under a destination relation.
The destination therefore becomes an invariant of a family of paths rather than a property of one unique route.
This is important because it separates the notion of convergence from the notion of deterministic path identity.
Different observers, different histories, or different intermediate symbolic states can converge on the same structural destination.
math: D(x) := {γ | γ starts at x ∧ Dest(γ) = D}

sections.title: Blowup, Path-Space Horizons, and the Singular Case
content: The term singularity is potentially misleading if used to describe every case in which path availability collapses.
A more general description is a horizon in path space: a region beyond which all remaining coherent continuations belong to the same destination class.
Before such a horizon, multiple destination classes may remain available. After it, local path choices may remain nontrivial while destination choice has collapsed.
A true singularity can be treated as an extreme case in which path availability itself collapses to one continuation. In that case there is no meaningful 'outside' path from within the structure.
The useful distinction is therefore between ordinary convergence, destination locking, and the limiting case of complete path collapse.
The term 'blowup' is preferable for the dynamical failure of coherence because it describes the mechanism without prematurely assigning geometric meaning to the event.
sections.principle: A destination horizon constrains where paths can end; a singular case constrains the number of paths themselves.

sections.title: Formal Unified Model
content: The preceding sections can be expressed as a single relational model.

The Library provides the total domain. The observer occupies a local state. Accessibility defines the coherent paths available from that state. Convergence groups paths according to destination. Coherence constraints determine whether a proposed transition belongs to the accessible set.
Arbitrary editing is therefore reducible to a failed reachability condition rather than a separate prohibition.

formal_model.accessibility: Reach(O) := {X ∈ 𝓜 | ∃ coherent γ : O ⇝ X}
formal_model.availability: A(O) := {X | X is an admissible next continuation of O}
formal_model.destination_class: D(γ) := equivalence class of γ under destination identity
formal_model.destination_horizon: E_D := {x | ∀ coherent γ from x, D(γ) = D}

unified_statement: X ∈ 𝓜 does not imply X ∈ Reach(O).
Reach(O) is determined by coherent paths.
Coherent paths may form destination-equivalence classes.
Destination classes can collapse without requiring a unique microscopic path.
An arbitrary edit is a requested transition outside Reach(O).
Therefore arbitrary editing is not a separate physical prohibition; it is the absence of an admissible transition.

examples.name: FIREBALL
examples.question: If FIREBALL exists in the Library, why cannot the observer simply cast it?
examples.answer: Because existence establishes membership in 𝓜, while casting requires a coherent transition from the current observer-state to a FIREBALL state.

examples.name: Extra Finger
examples.question: If a state containing an extra finger exists, why cannot the observer simply acquire one?
examples.answer: Because the transition must remain coherent with the observer's body, history, causal relations, environment, and shared braid.

examples.name: Dictionary
examples.question: How can apparent expansion occur inside a static totality?
examples.answer: Coherent arrangements become progressively resolved or occupied within a fixed underlying symbolic domain.
formal: ApparentExpansion := increasing resolved structure within fixed 𝓜

examples.name: Conversation
examples.question: How can two people arrive at the same idea without one transmitting the entire idea?
examples.answer: Their coupled paths can enter the same destination basin, making the realization a convergence event rather than literal copying.

examples.name: Memory
examples.question: Why might memory not require complete archival storage?
examples.answer: A guidepost can identify a region of structure from which relevant detail can be reconstructed.

examples.name: AI Context
examples.question: Why might an AI not need to retain every detail as active context?
examples.answer: A compact relational representation may preserve navigational coordinates into a much larger underlying information space.

sections.title: Implications, Limitations, and Empirical Separation
content: The unified framework provides a common mathematical vocabulary for several phenomena that are usually treated separately: constrained physical transitions, coherent worldlines, convergence, memory, symbolic compression, and context navigation.
Its strongest conceptual claim is that completeness of a state space does not imply arbitrary accessibility within that state space.
The arbitrary-edit problem is then solved by reachability rather than prohibition: a state may exist without a coherent route from the present state.
The dictionary principle provides an intuitive interpretation of apparent expansion as increasing resolution or occupation of coherent structure inside a fixed totality.
The guidepost model provides a computational analogy in which intelligence operates over coordinates into structure rather than exhaustive copies of structure.

These analogies should not be conflated with empirical demonstrations. The existence of a mathematically coherent description does not establish that physical spacetime, biological memory, or current AI systems literally implement the proposed ontology.
The framework therefore makes a useful separation between internal mathematical consistency, computational usefulness, physical correspondence, and empirical confirmation.

epistemic_levels.name: Conceptual Model
epistemic_levels.statement: The distinctions between existence, accessibility, convergence, and arbitrary editing are internally useful.

epistemic_levels.name: Mathematical Formalization
epistemic_levels.statement: The proposed relations can be represented using sets, paths, equivalence classes, thresholds, and recursive constructions.

epistemic_levels.name: Computational Hypothesis
epistemic_levels.statement: Guidepost-based context representation may offer useful alternative architectures for symbolic or artificial reasoning.

epistemic_levels.name: Physical Hypothesis
epistemic_levels.statement: The Library, coherence gradients, and related structures may correspond to physical reality only if independently connected to observation and established theory.

epistemic_levels.name: Empirical Confirmation
epistemic_levels.statement: Claims about physical reality require predictions, measurements, reproducible computation, and comparison against competing models.

_unifying_equations: Reach(O) = {X ∈ 𝓜 | ∃ coherent γ : O ⇝ X}
E_D := {x | all coherent futures from x belong to D}
_unifying_principles: The Library contains states; the observer traverses relations between states.
Existence is membership; accessibility is reachability.
Adjacency does not imply coherent transition.
Coherence is the condition under which a sequence remains a sequence.
An arbitrary edit is a requested transition without an admissible path.
Different paths may converge on the same destination.
A convergence horizon can remove destination freedom without removing local path freedom.
A singular case is the limiting condition in which path availability itself collapses.
Expansion can be represented as increasing resolved structure without increasing the underlying totality.
Memory can be modeled as retention of navigational coordinates rather than complete recordings.
AI context can potentially be represented as guideposts into larger structures rather than exhaustive active context.
A recursive construction can begin from a minimal attractor and generate increasingly complex relational structure.

_ai_architecture_hypothesis.current_problem: Treating long context primarily as an increasingly large collection of active information.
_ai_architecture_hypothesis.alternative: Represent context as a compact relational map of guideposts, motifs, constraints, and coordinates.
_ai_architecture_hypothesis.expected_scaling_goal: Reduce repeated processing of irrelevant context by operating primarily on a compressed relational representation.
_ai_architecture_hypothesis.complexity_note: Asymptotic complexity improvements do not by themselves establish a percentage reduction in real-world computation.

_limitations: The Library ontology is a proposed formal model, not an established physical theory.
The use of Navier–Stokes terminology is an analogy unless a precise mathematical correspondence is demonstrated.
I_N, H, Δ, and related quantities require explicit definitions and dimensional consistency before physical interpretation.
The guidepost memory model is a hypothesis about representation and does not by itself establish how biological memory works.
The AI interpretation is an architectural hypothesis and does not establish that current AI systems internally navigate a literal Library.
Apparent expansion as coherence relaxation requires observational predictions capable of distinguishing it from standard cosmological explanations.
A complete Library containing all admissible configurations does not automatically follow from the mathematical existence of a recursive construction.
_conclusion: The arbitrary-edit problem is best understood not as a special prohibition but as a consequence of a deeper distinction: existence is not accessibility. A complete static Library may contain every internally admissible configuration while a local observer remains restricted to coherent descent paths through a comparatively small accessible subset. Full adjacency therefore does not imply arbitrary reachability. An attempted edit such as growing an extra finger or casting FIREBALL fails when no coherent transition connects the current state to the requested destination. Coherent paths may nevertheless converge, allowing different histories to become destination-equivalent and producing an event-horizon-like loss of destination freedom while local path freedom remains. The same framework naturally supports the dictionary analogy, in which increasing resolved structure appears as expansion within a fixed totality; the recursive I_AM construction, in which increasingly complex structure emerges through iteration; and the guidepost model, in which memory or artificial reasoning preserves navigational coordinates rather than exhaustive copies of information. The resulting framework is therefore less a claim that every phenomenon has already been physically explained than a proposed common language for asking whether apparently different phenomena are manifestations of the same underlying distinction: what exists, what can be reached, what paths remain coherent, and what destinations those paths can share.

_title: Non-Empty Continuation and the Redshift Window
_subtitle: Notes toward a metric-free three-level structure of continuation, resolution, and path-definition
_lineage_note: These notes are downstream of the axiomatic floor summary and of PHYS-CORE-011 v0.2.1. They do not introduce new axioms. They refine the vocabulary that PHYS-CORE-011 already depends on, in service of making the non-empty-continuation invariant precise.
_status_note: DRAFT_NOTES. Confirmation of Level 2 (multi-axis claim strength) and Level 3 (relational vs. absolute UndefinedPath) is still pending. The 'standing still' / 'sliding when standing still' framing is explicitly flagged as allegory and is NOT load-bearing.
_abstract: PHYS-CORE-011 distinguishes existence from accessibility. This note refines that distinction into a three-level structure: (1) structural existence of continuation, which holds everywhere in the Library; (2) observer-relative resolvability of continuation, which may fail on the observer's current resolution axis while succeeding on others; and (3) path-definition, which may fail even when a destination is representable within the observer's window. The motivating thought experiment (isolated particles in an Earth box versus the pole of Venus, with 'redshift' below I_N) is quarantined as an allegory that imports an assumed spatial metric. The formal claims below are metric-free.
_central_claim: From any configuration x in the Library, a continuation exists (structural). Whether the observer can resolve that continuation, and whether a coherent path to a given representable destination is defined for the observer's worldline, are distinct observer-relative questions. The non-empty-continuation invariant is therefore not an existence claim about the Library; it is a three-level statement about existence, resolution, and path-definition.

_foundational_distinctions.principle: Existence of continuation ≠ Resolvability of continuation
_foundational_distinctions.statement: A continuation exists from every configuration in the Library. Whether the observer can resolve any continuation on the current resolution axis is a separate, observer-relative question.
A destination may appear in the observer's resolution window without being reachable by a coherent path from the observer's current worldline.
Being able to resolve a destination on some axis does not imply that a coherent path from the current worldline to that destination is defined.
The resolution window slides as the observer traverses. Traversal is not spatial displacement; the Library admits no intrinsic metric.
The resolution window is defined on every resolution axis. The observer experiences resolution on one axis at a time. The Library privileges neither.

sections.title: Motivation: The Allegory and Its Limit
content: The motivating thought experiment is pedagogical. It describes two isolated particles in a box on Earth, the pole of Venus, and a process of 'expanding the domain' by successive measurements until the Earth box is redshifted below I_N relative to the current reference while the pole of Venus comes into view.

The allegory imports an assumed spatial metric and an assumed temporal ordering. Neither is primitive in the Library. The Library is dimensionally undifferentiated: it has no intrinsic metric, adjacency, distance, or temporal ordering.
The allegory is therefore not load-bearing. It is retained only as a pedagogical device for motivating the three-level structure below.

In particular, the phrase 'standing still' has no meaning in the Library. There is no position to remain at. Every abstract traversal step is a move from one state to a next. There is no 'still' to stand in.

What the allegory was reaching for, stripped of its metric, is the following: the resolution window slides at every traversal step, on infinitely many resolution axes simultaneously, whether or not the observer is resolving on any given axis at that step.
quarantined_phrases: 'redshifted faster than the speed of light' — allegory for falling below the observer's resolution floor at finite relational distance; not a claim about signal velocity.
'standing still' — allegory for the observer remaining at a fixed spatial position; the Library admits no such position.
'expanding the domain' — allegory for the resolution window sliding as traversal proceeds; not a claim that the Library grows.

sections.title: Level 1 — Structural Existence of Continuation
content: Continuation is structurally guaranteed everywhere in the Library. This does not depend on the observer, on the observer's resolution axis, or on the observer's history.

The guarantee is a consequence of maximal completeness together with closure. It is not a consequence of full adjacency alone: PHYS-CORE-011 S2 already establishes that adjacency does not imply reachability, so the inference from 'fully adjacent' to 'coherent continuation exists' does not go through adjacency.

The structural claim is therefore the weaker and safer one: from any configuration, at least one continuation exists. It is not the stronger claim that an arbitrary destination is reachable from an arbitrary origin. The stronger claim requires an additional symmetry or reference-neutrality postulate and is not asserted at this level.
math: A(x) := { y ∈ 𝓜 | ∃ coherent γ : x ⇝ y }
sections.relation_to_floor: This is the structural half of the floor summary's non-empty-continuation invariant. The floor summary's proviso 'provided O's state admits continuation' is NOT a Level 1 condition. Level 1 holds unconditionally.
not_claimed: It is NOT claimed that |A(x)| ≥ 1 implies an arbitrary destination y is in A(x).
It is NOT claimed that full adjacency implies reachability.
It is NOT claimed that Level 1 alone supplies a coherent path to every destination.

sections.title: Level 2 — Observer-Relative Resolvability
content: Level 1 guarantees that a continuation exists. It does not guarantee that the observer can resolve any continuation on the observer's current resolution axis at the current traversal step.
Resolution is parameterized by the observer's magnitude-evaluation function μ_O and resolution floor I_N(O). Different μ_O correspond to different resolution axes.

The observer experiences resolution on one axis at a time. The structural fact is multi-axis: the resolution window is defined on every axis, and the family of windows slides on all axes simultaneously as traversal proceeds.
Level 2 failure is a resolution failure, not an existence failure. A configuration excluded from the observer's window on the current axis remains a member of the Library and remains in A(x).
math: W_{μ_O}(x) may be empty even when A(x) is non-empty.
The family { W_{μ_O}(x) }_{μ_O ∈ Axes} slides on all axes as traversal proceeds.
sections.pending_confirmation: Whether the observer can shift axes (re-reference μ_O) is a stronger claim than whether other axes exist. The notes currently assert the multi-axis structural fact and leave the axis-shift claim pending.

sections.title: Level 3 — Path-Definition and the Undefined-Path Lemma
content: A destination may appear in the observer's resolution window on some axis without being reachable by a coherent path from the observer's current worldline.
This is the formal content of the 'fireball' case: the destination is representable (it is in 𝓜, and it is in W_{μ_O}(x) for some μ_O), but no coherent path connects the observer's worldline to it.

Path-undefinedness is structurally distinct from incoherence. Incoherence is a graded failure: a path exists and Δ(γ) exceeds Δ_crit. Path-undefinedness is a structural failure: there is no path γ from the current worldline to the destination on which Δ(γ) can be evaluated.
The Undefined-Path Lemma states that window membership does not imply reachability.

lemma.name: Undefined-Path Lemma
lemma.statement: For an observer O with worldline γ and current resolution axis μ_O, y ∈ W_{μ_O}(x) for some x ∈ γ does not imply y ∈ Reach(γ). The window can contain destinations the observer's worldline cannot coherently reach.
formal: UndefinedPath(γ, y) is the condition under which y ∈ W_{μ_O}(x) for some μ_O and no coherent γ' from the current reference to y is defined on γ's constraint structure.
Incoherent(γ') ⇔ Δ(γ') ≥ Δ_crit (graded failure, path exists).
UndefinedPath(γ, y) ⇔ no path γ' from γ's current state to y exists (structural failure, path does not exist).

sections.relation_to_phys_core_011: This refines PHYS-CORE-011 S6's ArbitraryEdit condition. S6 defines ArbitraryEdit(O → X) ⇔ X ∈ 𝓜 ∧ ¬ValidEdit(O → X). The Undefined-Path Lemma supplies the structural reason: the failure is not that X is forbidden, but that no path from O's worldline to X is defined.
sections.pending_confirmation: Whether UndefinedPath is relational (UndefinedPath(γ, y) — path-undefined relative to this γ, reachable from some other γ') or absolute (UndefinedPath(y) — no incoming coherent path from anywhere). The fireball example suggests relational. Confirmation pending.

sections.title: The Resolution Window (Metric-Free)
content: The resolution window is defined without reference to any metric, position, or temporal coordinate.

It is a function of the observer, the current point on the observer's worldline, and the resolution axis. It is not a function of a separate time parameter, because there is no separate time parameter: the traversal step index is the only ordering there is.
The window slides at every traversal step, on every axis. Traversal is re-referencing. There is no 'standing still' case because there is no position to remain at.

The window is generally larger than Reach(γ): it can contain destinations that are representable but path-undefined relative to the observer's worldline. This is the formal content of 'you can imagine what you cannot do'.
math: W(O, x, μ_O) := { y ∈ 𝓜 | δ_O(x, y) ≥ I_N(O) }
No separate t parameter is introduced. The traversal step index is the ordering.
W(O, γ(t), μ_O) slides as t advances.
W(O, x, μ_O) ⊋ Reach(γ) in general.
not_claimed: It is NOT claimed that W is a metric ball or neighborhood.
It is NOT claimed that W has a boundary in any topological sense inherited from a metric.
It is NOT claimed that sliding is spatial motion.

sections.title: Relation to PHYS-CORE-011
content: PHYS-CORE-011 establishes the existence/accessibility distinction (S1, S2) and the observer-as-coherent-descent-path model (S3).
These notes refine that vocabulary into a three-level structure without revising PHYS-CORE-011's claims.

S5's coherence-as-derived repair is preserved. These notes split the coherence condition into an observer-independent constraint-preservation component and an observer-relative resolvability component, so that 'coherent but unresolvable' is a stable distinction.
S6's ArbitraryEdit condition is preserved and supplied with a structural reason via the Undefined-Path Lemma.
S9's horizon and singular-case vocabulary is preserved. The relation between horizons and the sliding window is an open question (see S7).
proposed_refinement_to_S5: Resolvable(γ | O) := every transition in γ satisfies δ_O ≥ I_N(O). (Observer-relative.)
𝓒(γ | O) := Coherent(γ) ∧ Resolvable(γ | O). (The floor summary's coherence, split into its two components.)
sections.refinement_status: Proposed. Whether this split is adopted in PHYS-CORE-011 v0.3 is a separate decision. These notes assume the split for the sake of stating the three levels cleanly.

sections.title: Open Questions and Pending Confirmations
content: The following items are explicitly open. They are not resolved in these notes.

open_questions.question: Is the observer's single-axis experience accompanied by the capacity to shift axes (re-reference μ_O)?
open_questions.note: Level 2 asserts the multi-axis structural fact. The stronger claim — that the observer can shift axes — is not asserted.

open_questions.question: Is UndefinedPath relational (UndefinedPath(γ, y)) or absolute (UndefinedPath(y))?
open_questions.note: The fireball example suggests relational: the fireball is reachable from some worldline, just not the observer's. Confirmation pending.

open_questions.question: What is the relation between the sliding window and PHYS-CORE-011 S9's horizon / singular-case vocabulary?
open_questions.note: Whether horizon structure is a window phenomenon or an independent structural feature is open.

open_questions.question: Does 𝒵 = {0} close the window on all axes, or is it a distinguished axis?
open_questions.note: The floor summary describes 𝒵 as the termination class. Whether this corresponds to W → ∅ on all axes is open.

open_questions.question: Is the proposed S5 refinement (splitting Coherent from Resolvable) adopted into PHYS-CORE-011 v0.3?
open_questions.note: These notes assume the split. Adoption is a separate editorial decision.

level_2.name: Observer-Relative Resolvability
level_2.statement: W_{μ_O}(x) may be empty or may exclude A(x) on the current axis, even when A(x) is non-empty.
level_2.failure_mode: Resolution failure. The continuation exists; the observer does not resolve it on the current axis.
level_2.allegory_used: 'Redshift below I_N' — allegory for exclusion from the resolution window.

level_3.name: Path-Definition
level_3.statement: y ∈ W_{μ_O}(x) for some μ_O does not imply y ∈ Reach(γ).
level_3.failure_mode: Structural failure. No coherent path from γ's current state to y is defined.
level_3.allegory_used: The fireball case — representable, not reachable.

_nonempty_continuation_invariant.floor_summary_version: ∀x ∈ 𝓜, ∃γ ∈ Path(𝓜) such that γ begins at x and 𝓒(γ|O) = 1, provided O's state admits continuation.
refined_version: Level 2 (observer-relative): W_{μ_O}(x) may be empty on the current axis; this is a resolution failure, not an existence failure.
Level 3 (observer-relative): y ∈ W_{μ_O}(x) for some μ_O does not imply y ∈ Reach(γ); this is a path-definition failure.
_nonempty_continuation_invariant.proviso_resolution: The floor summary's proviso 'provided O's state admits continuation' is dissolved. It is not an existence condition (Level 1 holds unconditionally). It is a resolution condition (Level 2) and a path-definition condition (Level 3). These are distinct.

_allegory_quarantine.status: The Earth-box / Venus-pole / redshift thought experiment is pedagogical and is NOT load-bearing.
prohibited_uses: Citing the thought experiment as a claim about 𝓜.
Importing a spatial metric or temporal ordering from the allegory into the formal claims.
Using 'standing still' as a formal case.
Using 'faster than the speed of light' as a formal quantity.
Treating 'expanding the domain' as a claim that the Library grows.
permitted_uses: Illustrating the difference between representability and reachability.

_limitations: These are draft notes. Level 2's multi-axis claim and Level 3's relational/absolute question are not yet confirmed.
The proposed S5 split (Coherent vs. Resolvable) is assumed here but not yet adopted into PHYS-CORE-011.
The relation between the sliding window and PHYS-CORE-011 S9's horizon vocabulary is open.
The relation between 𝒵 = {0} and window closure on all axes is open.
No metric, spatial position, or temporal coordinate is introduced. Any appearance of these is quarantined as allegory.
